input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Section 4.1 gives either Party a convenience termination right on 90 days' written notice against a one-year term with annual auto-renewal. The Company's 90 days' notice sits at the low end of the fallback (60–90 days), and HDI's mirror right is effectively exercisable only to stop a renewal on 90 days' notice, which also matches the fallback — neither is flagged. The material failure is Section 4.2(a): the Company's exit is not "without penalty" and the Termination Payment (12 months' Net Sales less $800,000, halved, payable in eight quarterly instalments) is uncapped and, on any realistic sales volume, dwarfs the fallback ceiling of three months' fees under Section 3.1. Given the revenue-share bargain and the negotiated $800,000 threshold, we adopt the fallback fee cap rather than deleting the payment outright.

proposal.summary: Cap the Termination Payment payable by the Company at three months' fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our playbook allows a convenience termination on 90 days' notice only where any early-termination fee is capped at three months' fees, and the Section 4.2 formula (12 months' Net Sales less $800,000, halved) is uncapped and far exceeds that. We have capped the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3.1 fees; we can discuss the cap level, but an open-ended exit penalty does not work for us.

ops.oldText: the balance of which shall be divided by two.
ops.newText: the balance of which shall be divided by two; provided, that in no event shall the Termination Payment exceed an amount equal to the fees paid by the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) calendar months immediately preceding the Termination Date.
